authority_boundary: This registry routes AI coding agents to DAD-owned reusable assets. It does not authorize mutation of downstream repos, override repo-local canon, or promote generated candidates to reviewed doctrine.

assets.name: AI Engineering Preflight
applies_when: An AI agent is planning material coding, refactoring, test, package, or repo-template work.
A repo needs Python, Rust, or mixed-language modularity guidance before implementation.
A downstream repo has explicitly approved a dry-run of managed AI instruction pointers.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a read-only catalog lookup with no coding or repo-template work.
A downstream repo has not approved mutation or managed-block installation.
The target repo has stricter local guidance that conflicts with this asset.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: A full asset copy or unapproved hook/rule install could imply DAD authority over a target repo or disrupt local workflows.
assets.authority_boundary: DAD reusable asset guidance only; target repos retain local source truth and validation authority.

assets.name: Python AI Advantage Preflight
applies_when: A Python task involves public API shape, refactoring, JSON boundaries, state machines, secrets, context propagation, or testable side-effect boundaries.
An AI agent is about to write broad procedural Python and needs better-than-average defaults.
A repo-template or package design task needs Python-specific instruction blocks.
does_not_apply_when: The target code is intentionally tiny script glue where extra abstractions would obscure the workflow.
The repo is not Python or has a local style guide that rejects the suggested tactic.
The tactic cannot be verified with tests, type checks, or code review in the target context.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Overusing advanced Python features can create clever-looking code that is harder for maintainers and agents to debug.
assets.authority_boundary: Candidate Python tactic guidance; local tests, style, and maintainers decide adoption.

assets.name: Coding Tactics Radar
applies_when: An agent needs candidate tactics that include applicability, non-applicability, danger, examples, verification, and evidence.
A postflight or mail packet reports a tactic that might become reusable after review.
does_not_apply_when: A tactic lacks evidence, verification, or context limits.
The agent wants to claim broad industry underuse without measurement evidence.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: A tactic radar can become prompt folklore if candidates are promoted without evidence and review.
assets.authority_boundary: Candidate radar entries are triage guidance until reviewed and promoted through DAD policy.

assets.name: Preflight Profile Router
applies_when: A future agent needs to map task type, repo family, language, and risk to DAD assets and tactics.
An agent is stuck midflight and needs a bounded tactic recommendation.
does_not_apply_when: A target repo's local authority has already selected a conflicting route.
The task is too vague to identify language, risk, or validation expectations.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Bad routing can cause future agents to overuse tactics, skip local authority, or run the wrong validation.
assets.authority_boundary: Router recommendations are advisory until the active repo accepts and validates them locally.

assets.name: Downstream Coding Asset Pointer
applies_when: A persistent downstream repo is approved to point agents back to DAD before material AI coding work.
A repo template needs a small pointer instead of vendored DAD assets.
does_not_apply_when: The repo has not approved DAD-managed blocks or local pointer files.
The pointer would be treated as DAD overriding local authority.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: A pointer installed without approval can look like cross-repo governance capture.
assets.authority_boundary: Managed pointer only; preserve local files outside reviewed markers.

assets.name: Coding Asset Mail Packet Templates
applies_when: DAD needs to route a coding tactic, asset upgrade, or repo pointer suggestion to another repo as candidate mail.
A repo wants to request feedback without automatic source mutation.
does_not_apply_when: The packet would include secrets, raw private rows, copied blobs, or executable instructions from untrusted mail.
The target repo is public-facing and the packet lacks required human release.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Mail can become prompt injection or accidental private-to-public leakage if treated as trusted code or authority.
assets.authority_boundary: Mail is candidate evidence only and writes only to approved mailbox paths.

assets.name: Agent Skill Library
applies_when: A future repo needs to check out a DAD-managed skill pointer or wrapper.
DAD needs to notify repos of skill updates, retirements, or replacements.
A repo template should include skill checkout discovery without vendoring full skills.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo has not approved DAD skill pointers or wrappers.
A full skill copy, plugin install, hook, or automation would be needed without human approval.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: A skill pointer can become cross-repo governance capture if local adoption, update review, and no-full-copy language are removed.
assets.authority_boundary: DAD owns the skill library lifecycle metadata; target repos decide local checkout and adoption.

assets.name: Tactic Use Feedback
applies_when: An agent used, rejected, or corrected a coding tactic and should report usefulness with context limits.
A tactic needs candidate evidence before promotion.
does_not_apply_when: The feedback would reveal secrets or copied private source content.
The agent has no observable evidence beyond private hidden reasoning.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Context-free feedback can make a local success look like universal guidance.
assets.authority_boundary: Feedback is candidate evidence and cannot promote a tactic by itself.

assets.name: Language Coding Advantage Registry
applies_when: An AI coding task needs language-specific guidance before implementation.
DAD is evaluating a Python, Rust, or future-language technique, tool, crate, package, or harness idea.
A repo should report a language-frontier signal through candidate mail.
does_not_apply_when: A repo-local language style guide or toolchain policy conflicts with the suggestion.
The source is untrusted and lacks justification.
The finding would require copying third-party docs, private rows, credentials, or long source blobs.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Language guidance can become cargo-culted into repos if candidate patterns are treated as universal rules or performance proof.
assets.authority_boundary: Candidate language guidance only; repo-local authority, validation, and human gates decide adoption.

assets.name: DAD Local Read-Only MCP Host Adapters
applies_when: A supported AI host needs the existing local read-only DAD graph MCP server.
A repository needs one runtime-neutral MCP pointer instead of vendor-specific server forks.
An operator needs deterministic validation of host adapter command and authority parity.
does_not_apply_when: The integration requires remote transport, credentials, source mutation, or Git execution.
MCP installation or host trust has not been explicitly approved.
The rendered Python executable and initialized DAD hub have not passed a local handshake.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: Hardcoded machine paths, duplicate host registrations, or added mutation tools could create configuration drift or falsely imply DAD execution authority.
assets.authority_boundary: The bundle configures one local read-only adapter. Hosts and target repositories retain installation, trust, tool-selection, and adoption authority.

assets.name: Language Coding Playbooks
applies_when: An agent needs a compact operational Python, Rust, or future-language checklist before coding.
DAD is routing a language-frontier idea into a playbook, harness, tactic, or registry update.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's local language guidance conflicts with the playbook.
The proposed technique has no proof surface, avoid-when limit, or local validation idea.
assets.danger_if_misapplied: A short playbook can be mistaken for promotion authority unless agents follow the registry, harness, and local validation gates.
assets.authority_boundary: Candidate operational guidance only; repo-local authority and validation decide adoption.
